title: Protocol for siRNA-mediated TET1 knockdown during differentiation of human embryonic stem cells into definitive endoderm cells
protocol: Add 1 mL of diluted Matrigel per well of a 6-well plate.
Let the plate sit at 37°C for 0.5–1 hour.
Retrieve cell cryovials from liquid nitrogen.
Roll the vial between gloved hands for 3-5 seconds to remove frost.
Immerse the cryovials quickly into a 37°C water bath, gently swirling them.
Thoroughly wipe the cryovials with 75% alcohol when only small ice crystals remain.
Transfer the contents of the cryovials to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Slowly add 5 mL of mTeSR1 medium containing 10 μM Y27632 to the cells in the 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Gently rock the tube back and forth to ensure stable osmotic pressure.
Centrifuge the cells at 250 g for 5 minutes.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant, removing as much as possible without disturbing the cell pellet.
Re-suspend the pellet by adding 1 mL of mTeSR1 medium containing 10 μM Y27632 and pipetting gently several times.
Aspirate Matrigel from the 6 well plate.
Slowly add all 1 mL of the hES cell suspension to the well.
Add an additional 1 mL of mTeSR1 medium containing 10 μM Y27632 to bring the total amount of medium to 2 mL.
Carefully slide the plate forward-to-back and side-to-side to ensure even cell distribution.
Place the plate into the 37°C incubator.
Observe cell growth under the microscope daily.
Replace 2 mL of fresh mTeSR1 medium without Y27632 for each well.
Pre-warm DMEM/F12 medium, 0.5 mM EDTA, and mTeSR1 medium at 15°C–25°C.
Add 1 mL of diluted Matrigel per well of 6 well plate.
Let the plate sit at 37°C for 0.5–1 h.
Observe cells under microscope before passaging and take pictures.
Aspirate supernatant from wells.
Wash cells with 1 mL of DMEM/F12 medium, then aspirate.
Add 1 mL of 0.5 mM EDTA to each well.
Incubate at 37°C for 5 min.
Observe digestion of the cells in each well under microscope.
Aspirate EDTA when bright gaps between cells are visible.
Add 1 mL of mTeSR1 medium to each well.
Gently pipette cells in an up-to-down, left-to-right sequence.
Aspirate the Matrigel from each well of the Matrigel plate.
Add 1.5 mL of mTeSR1 medium to each well and label with cell line name, passage number, and date.
Pipette the cell suspension into the wells at an appropriate ratio (usually 1:3 to 1:20).
Slide the plate forward-to-back and side-to-side to ensure even cell distribution.
Gently slide the plate once before placing it in the incubator.
Culture hES cells at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Observe cell growth daily under a microscope.
Replace 2 mL of fresh medium for each well when necessary.
Pre-warm DMEM/F12 medium, 0.5 mM EDTA, and mTeSR1 medium at 15°C-25°C before use.
Add 0.5 ml of diluted Matrigel per well in a 12-well plate and incubate for 0.5-1 h at 37°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from each well containing hES cells.
Wash with 1 ml of DMEM/F12 medium, aspirate, and add 1 ml of accutase to each well.
Incubate at 37°C for 7 min.
While hES cells are incubating with accutase, aspirate the Matrigel from each well of the Matrigel plate.
Add 1 ml of mTeSR1 medium containing 10 μM Y27632 to each well.
Observe digestion of cells under the microscope.
When bright gaps between cells are visible, add 1 mL mTeSR1 medium containing 10 μM Y27632 and gently pipette to generate single-cell suspension.
Transfer cell suspension to a 15 mL centrifuge tube and centrifuge at 250 g for 5 min.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant and add 1 mL mTeSR1 medium containing 10 μM Y27632, gently pipette to suspend cells.
Aspirate 20 μL of cell suspension and add 20 μL trypan blue dye to calculate number of viable cells.
Slowly pipette cell suspension into each well at a density of 400,000 cells per well of 12-well plate.
Slide the plate gently forward-to-back and side-to-side to ensure even distribution of cells.
Place the plate in the incubator and culture at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Prepare D1 medium by mixing RPMI1640 base medium, Activin A (final concentration: 100 ng/mL), CHIR99021 (final concentration: 3 μM), and BSA (final concentration: 5 mg/mL).
The next day (denoted as D0), confirm cell growth under the microscope.
Replace the medium in each well with 1 mL of D1 induction medium.
On Day 1, remove the D1 induction medium from each well and add 1 mL of D2 induction medium.
On Day 2, remove the D2 induction medium from each well and add 1 mL of D3 induction medium.
On Day 3, proceed to examine cell morphology under microscopy.
Discard the medium in each well.
Wash cells with 2 mL of 1× PBS.
Detach cells using 1 mL of EDTA at 37°C for 5 min.
Pipette up and down several times to disperse the cells.
Transfer detached cells to a 1.5 mL EP tube.
Centrifuge at 250 g for 5 min.
Discard the EDTA solution carefully with pipette.
Add 1 mL of Trizol to each cell sample.
Pipette vigorously several times to lyse the cells.
Perform RNA isolation immediately or store at -80°C.
Add 200 μL chloroform to the sample.
Mix the sample thoroughly by repeated inversion.
Incubate for 2 min at 15°C–25°C.
Repeat the above step three more times.
Centrifuge at 12000 rpm (∼ 13000 g) for 15 min at 4°C.
Prepare a new EP tube containing 400 μL of isopropanol and place it on ice.
Pipette 400 μL of the top transparent liquid (aqueous phase) and transfer it to the pre-chilled isopropanol.
Mix thoroughly by repeated inversion for 15 s, then place on ice and incubate for 10 min.
Centrifuge at 12000 rpm (∼13000 g) for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully without removing the precipitate.
Add 700 μL of pre-cooled 75% ethanol to the precipitate.
Invert the mixture several times to thoroughly wash the precipitate.
Centrifuge at 12000 rpm (about 13000 g) for 5 min at 4°C, then discard the supernatant.
Centrifuge at 12000 rpm (about 13000 g) for 3 min.
Carefully remove residual ethanol completely using a micropipette.
Allow the precipitate to air-dry for 10 min at 15°C–25°C.
Dissolve the precipitate in an appropriate amount of RNase-free water.
Incubate at 55°C for 10 minutes.
Measure the concentration of isolated RNA using a NanoDrop.
Assess the quality of isolated RNA by gel electrophoresis.
Store the RNA at −80°C for several months.
Synthesize cDNA using the PrimeScript RT Master Mix kit, following manufacturer’s instructions.
Keep RNA on ice during mix preparation.
Gently mix the reaction solution before performing the reverse-transcription reaction.
Start the cDNA synthesis program as specified in the protocol.
Perform qPCR experiments using the ChamQ Universal SYBR qPCR Master Mix kit, following manufacturer’s instructions.
Dilute the cDNA synthesized in step 6 to a concentration of 1/10 for use.
Prepare the qRT-PCR mix as indicated.
Pipette 7.5 μL of the qRT-PCR mix into each well of a 96-well white plate.
Pipette 2.5 μL of primer mix to each well.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate at 4000 rpm for 2 min at 4°C in a centrifuge equipped with a suited rotor.
Load the 96-well plate into the Real-Time PCR Detection System.
Start the PCR program as shown in Table 5.
Calculate relative expression using the “ΔCt” method.
Dissolve siRNA with RNAse-free water to a concentration of 20 μM.
Transfect cells using Lipofectamine™ RNAiMAX kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
For each transfection, prepare the lipid dilution as specified in Table 6.
Dilute siRNA as indicated in Table 7.
Add 7.5 μL of NC siRNA directly for negative control.
Mix the diluted siRNA with the lipid solution (1:1 ratio) and incubate for 5 minutes at 15°C–25°C.
Perform the first round of transfection when cells are seeded by adding the siRNA-lipid mixture to cells.
After 8 hours, aspirate the medium containing siRNA and replace it with fresh mTeSR1 medium (containing 10 μM Y27632).
Incubate for another 16 hours before replacing the medium with D1 induction medium.
Simultaneously perform a second round of transfection by adding the siRNA-lipid mixture to cells.
After an additional 8 hours, aspirate the medium containing siRNA-lipid mixture and replace it with fresh D1 induction medium.
Incubate for 24 hours before replacing the D1 medium with D2 induction medium.
Culture cells in D2 medium for another 24 hours before switching to D3 medium.
Continue culturing the cells for an additional 24 hours to complete the DE induction process.
Check cell morphology under a microscope to confirm ES cells have been successfully induced to DE cells.
Collect cell samples according to step 4.
Perform RNA isolation and cDNA synthesis according to steps 5 and 6, respectively.
Perform qRT-PCR according to step 7 to examine the efficiency of siRNA knockdown.
Evaluate the impact of siRNA on LTR6B expression and DE induction.
Isolate genomic DNA using TIANamp Genomic DNA Kit, following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Measure the concentration of genomic DNA in a NanoDrop.
Perform bisulfite conversion.
Perform bisulfite conversion of genomic DNA using EpiTect Fast Bisulfite Conversion Kits, following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Use 1 μg of genomic DNA for each sample in the conversion process.
Thaw 10× La Buffer and dNTPs on ice for PCR setup.
Set up PCR reaction according to the provided table instructions.
Perform PCR using a programmed thermal cycler as specified in Table 9.
Load the PCR products along with a nucleic acid stain (e.g., SYBR Gold) and tracking dye such as Bromophenol Blue.
Add a suited DNA Ladder for size reference.
Run electrophoresis in 1× TAE buffer at 120 V, for 30 min.
Visualize DNA fragments on a UV gel imaging system.
Excise the DNA fragments with a size of 263 bp using a clean razor blade.
Transfer the excised gel slices into a clean 1.5 mL EP tube.
Purify DNA from gel pieces using a HiPure Gel DNA Mini Kit.
Ligate purified PCR product into pMD18-T vector.
Incubate ligation reaction at 16°C for 4 hours.
Turn on water bath and set temperature to 42°C.
Thaw required amount of E. coli competent cells (DH5α) on ice.
Add all ligation reaction to 30 μL competent cells kept on ice.
Gently tap tube.
Incubate mixture on ice for 30 minutes.
Place competent cells in water bath at 42°C and heat shock for 45 seconds.
Immediately place heat-shocked competent cells on ice for 3 minutes.
Add 200 μL pre-warmed LB liquid medium without antibiotic to cells.
Incubate cells in shaking incubator at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Spread 7 μL IPTG and 40 μL X-gal evenly on surface of LB agar plate.
Plate the transformation mixes onto LB agar plates with ampicillin antibiotics using a sterile loop.
Incubate at 37°C for ∼16 hours in a bacterial incubator.
Check the growth of bacterial colonies on the agar plates.
Prepare sterile EP tubes and add 500 μL of LB liquid medium with ampicillin antibiotic to each tube.
Pick a white colony using a sterile 10 μL pipette tip, transfer it into the LB liquid medium in the EP tube, agitate several times, and discard the tips.
Incubate these tubes in a shaker at 37°C in 200 rpm for ∼16 hours.
Perform Sanger Sequencing using a universal primer M13F or M13R at a commercial sequencing facility.
Analyze sequencing results.
